MET 2026-09-15, graded conjunct-by-conjunct against the wired bridge; supersedes the ABSENT grading of 2026-09-13, every conjunct of which was accurate when written.

C1 a declared client input request: MET. The stdio caller context reads the per-request declaration (`src/gateway/server/mod.rs:3061`, `input_capabilities: request_shape.declared_capabilities()`) instead of the hardcoded `Declared::NONE` the prior grading cited; the row's client declares `elicitation` in `_meta.clientCapabilities` on every call.

C2 reaches a legacy stdio client: MET. Wiring: the serve loop builds the real `StdioClientChannel` over the single writer task's sender (`src/gateway/server/mod.rs:2403`, `spawn_stdio_writer` at :129) and passes it to every non-`initialize` dispatch; `NoClientChannel` survives only on the batch and test paths that have no writer to queue on (:2467, :2527). The production call site is `src/gateway/meta_mcp/invoke.rs:2107`, which now admits a caller whose `principal_fingerprint` is `None` -- every stdio caller -- alongside the legacy era it already admitted, and runs `InputBridge::run` inside the call. That predicate also admits an anonymous caller on a transport with no client channel: it too has no `principal_fingerprint`. Such a caller cannot be asked, so the bridge returns `DeliveryError::NoSession` before anything reaches the wire. On the modern era the call site falls through to the mint rather than failing, which is what keeps the ratified `-32003` of `unbindable_continuation` reaching that caller instead of a `-32603` from `bridge_failed`; on the legacy era it still fails, because a 2025 client cannot redeem a continuation and an envelope it cannot present is worse than an error. Both halves are pinned -- `an_unnameable_caller_is_not_offered_an_interim_exchange` and `a_legacy_caller_with_no_live_channel_cannot_be_asked`, `src/gateway/meta_mcp/tests.rs:3958` and `:3985`.

C3 the answer reaches the backend: MET and asserting. `ac_mrtr_7a_stdio_client_answers_while_serve_loop_reads` (`tests/mik_7212_mrtr7_stdio_acs.rs:414`) spawns the shipped binary over two pipes, answers the outbound `elicitation/create`, and asserts the backend's post-answer payload (`"answered"`) parsed out of the `gateway_invoke` envelope.

C4 the gateway keeps reading: MET. Non-`initialize` dispatch is spawned off the reader (`mod.rs:2546`) and the reader routes the client's reply back by id while that dispatch is outstanding (`mod.rs:2438`). Were it still inline the row would deadlock rather than fail.

Second falsifier, on the fall-through rather than the wiring, and run involuntarily in both directions, because two successive cuts of this change were wrong in opposite ways. (a) With no `NoSession` arm at all -- `bridge_failed` on every bridge error -- `cargo test --all-features` reported `4950 passed; 1 failed`, the failure being `an_unnameable_caller_is_not_offered_an_interim_exchange` (`src/gateway/meta_mcp/tests.rs:3958`) on `left: -32603, right: -32003`. (b) With the arm present but not qualified by era, the same command reported `4950 passed; 1 failed`, the failure being `a_legacy_caller_with_no_live_channel_cannot_be_asked` (`:3985`), which requires the delivery failure to stay a failure for a client that cannot redeem a continuation. Neither is in the five-mutant sweep above: every member of that sweep perturbed the stdio transport, and none perturbed the predicate that admits callers to it.

Regraded 2026-09-12: the 2026-09-12 MET grade is WITHDRAWN. It was established by module, not conjunct by conjunct, off a passing test count. A conjunct audit splits the criterion into seven parts and two of them have no covering construct. COVERED: principal/backend/resource keying for load (s01_independent_committed_fixture_resolves_every_account_axis, store_tests.rs:166), for save (s03_explicit_initialization_creates_encrypted_authority_and_reopens, tests.rs:272) and for refresh (invalidate_during_held_refresh_discards_stale_provider_success, service_refresh_tests.rs:102); at-rest protection (s02_envelope_roundtrip_has_exact_public_shape_and_no_plaintext_secrets, tests.rs:168 and s03_independent_aes256_gcm_vector_opens_exact_expired_payload, tests.rs:362, against seal_bytes at storage.rs:154 with 0o600 at commit.rs:81); no silent loss under crash (s10_a_committed_generation_survives_an_abrupt_death, crash_tests.rs:119). NOT COVERED: existing single-user data is READABLE - no test opens a pre-existing 3.x single-user store; and MIGRATED - no test, no code path, and the source states the opposite. src/personal_accounts/mod.rs:779 reads "Existing state is never replaced, and nothing is migrated into a store this command creates" and :790 "a store this creates has zero records by construction"; src/commands/upgrade.rs:243 ships the user-facing notice "Stored tokens from 3.x are not migrated: each OAuth backend re-authenticates once". legacy_migration (mod.rs:207) is a dead field, only ever written None (repair_tests.rs:179). This is an implementation gap, not a test gap: the row cannot reach MET by adding tests. Either the migration path is built, or the criterion is rewritten to match the shipped re-authenticate-once behaviour, which is an operator decision. The accounts_init_store.rs:117 local-only failure recorded by the previous note is unrelated and stands. Follow-up 2026-09-12: the two options are not symmetric, and the source says which way it leans. Not migrating is a deliberate shipped commitment, not an omission: it is item 1 of four in NOTICE_4_0_0_ITEMS (src/commands/upgrade.rs:241), a constant the comment at :238 says is pinned as a slice "so a test can assert the notice still carries every item". Building a migration therefore does not merely add a code path; it falsifies a release note the operator has already published to users and would have to be withdrawn from the notice, and it needs 3.x token material to be decryptable by 4.0.0 code that no longer keeps that format. Rewriting the criterion to match the shipped re-authenticate-once behaviour costs one requirement edit and leaves every other conjunct as graded. The recommendation is the rewrite; the decision is still the operator's, because it changes what MIK-6744 promised. Follow-up 2026-09-13: the asymmetry is now verified at source rather than inferred, and the recommendation is to rewrite the criterion. There is no 3.x store reader and no legacy key-derivation path anywhere in src/personal_accounts/: legacy_migration (mod.rs:207) is propagated by commit.rs:285-299 and written None at repair_tests.rs:179 and nowhere else, so the migration option is not a design alternative but unwritten decryption for key material this release cannot read. Against that, NOTICE_4_0_0_ITEMS (upgrade.rs:241) is pinned as a slice with the comment at :238 stating it is a slice so a test can assert the notice still carries every item, and item 1 is the no-migration promise the operator has already published. Building migration therefore falsifies a test-pinned shipped commitment. An implementing agent declined to write a test for this row on 2026-09-13 and was correct to: a test pinning the shipped behaviour asserts the opposite of the criterion, and a test pinning migration is red by construction. The row stays pending because rewriting a release criterion is a scope decision and is not an agent's to land.

The A/B-versus-C/D/E comparison is void by construction rather than by suspicion: the two sides ran different experiments. 3.5.0 and 3.5.1 serve the workload from cache with or without MCP headers, while 4.0.0 caches only when the MCP-Protocol-Version header is present, and the k6 harness never sends it, so the baseline arms answered from cache while the 4.0.0 arms did backend work and were then throttled by the shipped 100 rps default that the pinned config never overrides. Ratifying this row means eliminating the cache divergence, not raising the rate limit.

Cause located, and it is deliberate rather than a regression: cache_protocol_revision (src/protocol/meta.rs:514) keys the cache by protocol revision and returns None when the revision cannot be identified, which the doc comment at :512 states is fail-closed and means skip cache. A legacy-shaped request falls to accepted_legacy_revision(header) and then to the session revision (:523); a stateless POST carrying neither yields None and is never cached. 4.0.0 is the correct half of this divergence -- 3.5.x cached responses for requests that declared no revision at all, so one entry could be served across revisions. The release-readiness consequence is an upgrade surprise rather than a defect: any 3.5.x client that neither sends the header nor initializes a session loses caching entirely on upgrade and puts that traffic onto its backends. That belongs in the 4.0.0 release notes and the upgrade migration, and is recorded in neither today.
